findings.title: enableSqlExpressions consults the feature flag but both branches return false (dead, inverted logic)
findings.body: `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (note the variable is true when the flag is *disabled*) and then returns `false` in both the `if enabled` branch and the fall-through. The flag lookup is therefore a no-op and the naming is inverted. If the intent is to hard-disable SQL expressions (as the PR title says), the function should simply return false / the `case QueryTypeSQL` should return the error directly, with a comment referencing the CVE. As written, the code looks like a botched feature-flag gate, and a future maintainer is likely to 'fix' the inverted condition and silently re-enable the code path that led to CVE-2024-9264. Security-critical kill switches should not be expressed as misleading dead logic.

findings.title: Legacy path reports disabled feature as a user SQL error ('sql-invalid-sql' / 'error reading SQL command')
findings.body: `NewSQLCommand` (used by the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`buildCMDNode` path as well as the new reader) now always fails because `sql.TablesList` calls the stubbed `RunCommands`, which unconditionally returns 'not implemented'. The failure is surfaced as `errutil.BadRequest("sql-invalid-sql", WithPublicMessage("error reading SQL command"))` and logged as `"invalid sql query"` at Warn level. Users (and support) will be told their SQL is malformed when the real cause is that the feature has been disabled for security reasons, and the error ID/message is inconsistent with the `"sqlExpressions is not implemented"` error returned from `ReadQuery`. Return an explicit 'SQL expressions are disabled' error (and skip `TablesList` entirely) so the two entry points behave consistently and the message is truthful.

findings.title: TablesList always fails via the stub but still builds a DuckDB command and logs at Error level with user SQL
findings.body: With `NewInMemoryDB()` now returning a stub whose `RunCommands` always errors, `TablesList` can never succeed, yet it still escapes the input, formats the DuckDB-specific `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` string, calls the stub, and then logs `logger.Error("error serializing sql", ..., "sql", rawSQL, "cmd", cmd)` on every invocation. Every attempt to use a SQL expression (including probes by attackers) now produces guaranteed Error-level log lines containing user-controlled SQL, and the surrounding `tablesFromAST`/`astError`/`existsInList` code is unreachable dead code. The variable is also still named `duckDB` even though the PR says it removes DuckDB references. The function should short-circuit with a clear 'disabled' error (or the whole file should be reduced to that) instead of going through an always-failing DuckDB-shaped path.

findings.title: No regression test asserting SQL expressions are rejected on either entry point
findings.body: This PR is the in-repo fix for a critical RCE/LFI (CVE-2024-9264), but it adds no tests. There is no test that `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` returns an error for `QueryTypeSQL` (with and without `FlagSqlExpressions` enabled), no test that the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` path fails, and no test that `sql.NewInMemoryDB().QueryFramesInto` / `RunCommands` return 'not implemented'. Without such tests, a later refactor (e.g. 'fixing' the inverted logic in `enableSqlExpressions`, or restoring a real `DB` implementation) could re-expose the vulnerable path unnoticed. Any pre-existing tests in `pkg/expr/sql` or `pkg/expr` that exercised `TablesList`/`NewSQLCommand` with valid SQL and expected success also need to be updated or removed, as they would now fail against the stub.

findings.title: sqlExpressions feature flag remains registered/documented (as enabling DuckDB) and the UI still offers the SQL type, but the backend now always rejects it
findings.body: After this change the backend unconditionally rejects SQL expressions regardless of `FlagSqlExpressions`, but the flag is still registered in the feature registry with a description along the lines of 'Enables using SQL and DuckDB functions', is still listed in the feature-toggles documentation, and the frontend still exposes the SQL expression type when the flag is on. Operators who enable the flag will get a working UI option that always fails with 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' / 'error reading SQL command'. The PR description acknowledges leaving docs untouched, but at minimum the flag description and docs should state that the feature is disabled (and no longer DuckDB-based), or the flag should be marked as non-functional, so users are not misled into enabling a dead toggle.
